title: Void Ending in a Trine to Mercury
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The trine is the best of the aspects, the one the doctrine uses to tie the Moon to the fortunes. The text grades it as perfect friendship, because the signs it joins are of one element and gaze at each other in full agreement; works meant to endure are founded with the Moon fixed, and the lord of her house regarding her in trine or sextile.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a trine to Mercury, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his quicksilver turn of mind. Mercury is intellect's planet: learning, dialectic, geometry, astronomy, writing, and the reading of tongues, with every craft found by subtle talent under his governance. He rules the tongue, the brain, and the sensory memory, and quicksilver among the metals. The electional doctrine guards him closely: a work founded on Mercury must not find him retrograde, burning in the Sun's beams, or under an unfortunate planet's gaze.
